r20Gap.recordedIn: index.ts composition doc (:20492-20515) and this evidence
r20Gap.escapingOnly: the transport edge observes only failures that ESCAPE the route handlers; handled failures are translated per route before the request promise settles and never reach it
r20Gap.coarseClassification: the edge calls recordError, which records every escape as the coarse code "error" at level error; the Fail/Die/Interrupt classification lives in observe/recordCause and is not wired to this edge (the transport boundary is async/Promise, not an Effect)
r20Gap.clientEscapes: a client-caused escape (a 4xx-ish BridgeHttpError that escapes a route) is counted as a module failure; there is no client-vs-module classification at the edge
whatR20StillNeeds: an Effect boundary at the request entry (or per-route hooks with ONE report owner) so handled failures are observable without approximating
classification of Fail/Die/Interrupt at the report edge instead of the coarse error code
separation of client-caused escapes from module failures (or a status/class field on the edge)
